items.criterion: The random point charge experiment demonstrates that the Latent Ewald Summation (LES) method can recover exact atomic charges from energy and force data alone. Using a dataset of 128-atom configurations with fixed +1e and -1e charges, we train a CACE model that predicts both energies/forces and latent charges. The resulting plots show learning curves, test-set force errors, and a charge parity scatter plot, confirming that the model accurately extracts electrostatic information without any charge labels.

Using two molecules with net charges +1e and -1e at varying distances, the CACE model trained on distorted dimer configurations reproduces the reference binding energy curve almost exactly, demonstrating that LES correctly handles non-local Coulomb interactions.

items.criterion: The Ag₃ cluster experiment shows that the framework can distinguish potential energy surfaces corresponding to different total charge states (+1 and -1) without explicit charge labels. By training separate CACE models on each charge state (or using a global charge embedding), the predicted energy–bond length curves correctly separate the two surfaces and match the reference Morse+Coulomb model, validating the method's ability to learn charge-dependent physics.
